newsitem.title: USA: Weyerhaeuser Co pulp mill in US EPA program.
newsitem.headline: Weyerhaeuser Co pulp mill in US EPA program.

text.p: A Georgia pulp mill owned by Weyerhaeuser Co will go through an environmental overhaul under a voluntary federal program that gives industries more leeway in meeting pollution standards if they increase public health and environmental protections.
The Environmental Protection Agency said Friday it signed an agreement with Weyerhaeuser for its Flint River pulp mill in Oglethorpe, Ga.
The agreement is the first for a forest products facility under the EPA's Project XL pilot program which allows industries more flexibility in meeting environmental rules.
The plan for the Weyerhaeuser plant, which already meets EPA water pollution standards, was developed with involvement of local citizens, the EPA said.
Under the plan, the plant is to reduce daily water use to about 10 million gallons, while the industry mill average is 25 million.
It also is to have a 50 percent reduction in wastewater from its bleach plant, reducing the amount of chlorine compounds and pollutants discharged into the river.

The company also is to enhance wildlife habitat on about 300,000 acres of its forest lands, and is to update the mill's environmental management system to minimize end-of-pipeline cleanup or treatment.
